claim: match/2 emits each element of the private primitive's result array, while test/2 returns the primitive boolean directly.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: The one-argument match, test, and capture overloads accept a pattern string or a nonempty array containing pattern and optional modifiers; other forms raise a jq error.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: capture reduces only named capture records into an object, preserving null for an unmatched named group and resolving a repeated name by later capture-array order.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: scan forces global matching and emits the whole matched string when there are no groups, otherwise an array of capture strings in numeric group order.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: splits forces global matching and emits the character-indexed slices between ordered matches; split collects that stream into one array.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: sub reduces matches in order, evaluates the replacement filter against an object of named captures, supports replacement streams, appends the remaining suffix, and returns the input unchanged when there is no match.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: gsub delegates to sub after appending g to the caller flags, so duplicate g modifiers are accepted and replacement-stream Cartesian behavior belongs to the jq-coded wrapper.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: The native primitive requires a string input and pattern, accepts only string or null modifiers, and reports distinct runtime errors for each wrong type.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: The supported modifiers are g for repeated search, i for ignore case, x for extended syntax, m for multiline-dot behavior, s for single-line anchors, p for m plus s, l for longest, and n for nonempty matches; any other codepoint rejects the whole modifier string.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Patterns compile with UTF-8 encoding, Perl-NG syntax, and capture groups enabled; compile failures are surfaced with the exact Oniguruma message prefixed by Regex failure:.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Test mode initializes false, returns true at the first match without constructing capture records, and does not use g to enumerate later matches.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Each non-test result is an object with offset, length, string, and captures; capture records have offset, length, string, and name in numeric group order.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Match and capture offsets and lengths are Unicode codepoint counts computed from Oniguruma byte spans; combining codepoints count separately rather than as one grapheme.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: An unmatched group is represented by offset -1, length 0, string null; a participating empty group has its character offset, length 0, and string empty.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Oniguruma name iteration assigns a name to every referenced numeric capture slot; the capture array remains in numeric group order even when a name is repeated.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Global search appends matches in ascending non-overlapping search order and resumes at the previous match end for nonempty matches.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: After a zero-width match jq advances the next search start by exactly one byte and continues while start is at most end; this prevents one lookahead from repeating but can expose duplicate codepoint offsets over multibyte input.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: A search failure other than mismatch discards accumulated results and returns an Oniguruma message prefixed by Regex failure:; mismatch terminates normally.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Without HAVE_LIBONIG the primitive consumes its arguments and raises one stable unavailable-library error covering match, test, sub, and related functions.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: The evaluator-visible native surface is one four-argument _match_impl C function; match, test, capture, scan, splits, split, sub, and gsub are jq-coded builtins layered above it.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Pinned fixtures require codepoint offsets for combining and multibyte UTF-8 and require combining marks to contribute to length.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Pinned fixtures require empty global matches at every ASCII position, n to suppress them, and different records for unmatched versus participating-empty named groups.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Pinned fixtures require global match and scan output in left-to-right order, with scan groups emitted in capture order.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Pinned fixtures cover first-only sub, global gsub, named replacement context, zero-width replacements, greedy versus lazy matching, Unicode replacement, and replacement filters that emit multiple values.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: Pinned fixtures require leading and trailing empty pieces, no-match passthrough, case-insensitive delimiters, streamed splits, and suppression of empty delimiters with n.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: jv_string_sized validates UTF-8 and replaces each badly encoded unit with U+FFFD, so byte input converted through that constructor is normalized before regex matching can observe it.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: The jq CLI lowers Oniguruma's process-global parse-depth limit to 1024 before compiling or executing filters.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: The jq build prefers a requested or system Oniguruma, falls back to the bundled source, supports disabling regex, and only adds regex fixtures when Oniguruma is enabled.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: When bundled Oniguruma is selected, libjq and jq both link its libonig and the build recurses into the vendor directory.
author: codex-specialty-regex

claim: After every zero-width match jq advances the next search cursor by one byte, permits the cursor through the byte-length endpoint, and passes it directly to Oniguruma; neither the cursor nor a returned empty position is required to be a UTF-8 boundary.
author: codex-specialty-regex-boundary-fixer

claim: jq converts a zero-width raw byte position by decoding complete codepoints while the decoding pointer is less than that position, so different raw positions inside or at the end of one multibyte codepoint can report the same codepoint offset without reducing result cardinality.
author: codex-specialty-regex-boundary-fixer

claim: Nonempty whole matches and captures use the Oniguruma begin/end byte ranges to derive codepoint offsets and lengths and to copy their matched bytes; these ranges are distinct from the bytewise search cursor and empty-result positions.
author: codex-specialty-regex-boundary-fixer
